book-of-etiquette-volume-ii: Lillian Eichler's famous guide to manners continues with advice on weddings, dinners, letters, and social life. The book that taught America how to behave covers every occasion with calm authority. A fascinating look at the rules of polite society. Her calm, clear rules guided millions of readers through the social maze of the twentieth century.
a-half-century-of-conflict-volume-ii: Parkman's magisterial history of the French and English struggle for North America continues in this second volume. Frontier wars, great sieges, and the clash of empires unfold with his unmatched narrative power and deep research. Essential reading for all who love the colonial story.
the-guide-to-reading-the-pocket-universi: Lyman Abbott edits this guide to reading — essays on books, authors, and the art of getting the most from literature. Part of the Pocket University series, it aimed to bring college wisdom to every home. A wise companion for the self-taught reader. Practical counsel on choosing and digesting books fills these helpful pages.
ma-rkandeya-pura-na-books-vii-and-viii: B. Hale Wortham translates Books VII and VIII of the Mârkandeya Purâna — ancient Sanskrit tales of gods, kings, and cosmic ages. These sacred stories open a window onto classical Hindu imagination. A pioneering English rendering of a great text. Wortham's careful English opens these old Sanskrit wonders to new readers.
expositions-of-holy-scripture-st-matthew: Alexander Maclaren opens Matthew, chapters nine to twenty-eight — tales of mercy, hard sayings, and the road to the cross. His warm, wise words have fed souls for a hundred years. A treasure of old evangelical teaching. Preachers still turn to Maclaren for light on hard texts.
egyptian-tales-translated-from-the-papyr: Petrie's second series brings tales of the XVIIIth and XIXth dynasties — the age of Tutankhamun and Rameses the Great. Ghost stories, adventures, and magic from ancient Thebes, three thousand years old. Still thrilling after all these millennia. Petrie's spade and pen brought dead centuries back to life.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abstemii: A 1913 entry on the abstemii — those who from nature cannot take wine, and the Church's care for them. Joseph Gignac states the old rulings. Even the chalice yields to human weakness. Canon law with a human face. Mustum, unfermented juice, served their need.
